title: In vitro properties of large serine integrase hybrids derived from ϕC31 and TG1 integrases.
data_url: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13425240/ (no repository deposit; the only data is Table 1 inside the article)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: There are no data files to open. I read the complete open-access full text from Europe PMC and transcribed its only quantitative table (Table 1): 8 att-site conditions x 4 integrases = 32 cells, 4 of them 'ND' (not done), so 28 numeric recombination percentages. I confirmed no supplement exists (Europe PMC hasSuppl='N'; the supplementaryFiles endpoint returned HTTP 500) and no deposit exists (Zenodo/Dryad DOI search returned 0 hits; the only accessions in the text are two NCBI protein records, UZP69254.1 for TG1 integrase and BAM36534.1 for phiC31 integrase). The publisher page at academic.oup.com returned HTTP 403.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That each Table 1 value is a mean over triplicate gel-band quantifications with a standard deviation printed under the gel lanes in Figures 5, 6, 8 and 9; I did not read the per-lane standard deviations because they are rendered inside figure images, not text. The att-site DNA sequences themselves are also only shown inside figure images (Figures 4C, 7B, 9B), so I could not verify them as machine-readable text.

a1_downloadable.note: Marginal pass: the article is open access (CC BY-NC) and its single data table is readable in the Europe PMC/PMC full text, but there is no deposited dataset anywhere. Data availability statement reads 'All the data underlying this article are contained within the article.' Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI: 0 hits.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The label — percent of starting plasmid substrate converted to recombination product — is printed directly in Table 1, one value per integrase x att-site pair. No construction or inference needed; it just has to be retyped from the article.

a3_inputs_present.note: Partial fail: the four protein sequences are retrievable from two NCBI accessions (trivial), but the att-site DNA sequences — the actual varying input — exist only as coloured letters inside figure images (Figures 4C, 7B, 9B). They would have to be hand-transcribed from pictures. Only ~10 sites, so tedious rather than impossible, but nothing is machine-readable.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are explicit: 'All values are expressed as percentage of starting substrate converted to product', measured by agarose-gel band densitometry corrected for fragment molecular weight. Consistent across the whole table.

a5_enough_rows.note: FATAL. Table 1 is the entire dataset: 8 att-site conditions x 4 integrases = 32 cells, minus 4 'ND', leaves 28 measured percentages. Even counting every gel lane in Figures 5-9 separately, the total is a few dozen. The checklist threshold is ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: 28 numbers and ~10 short DNA sequences. Fits anywhere; this is the only killer it passes comfortably.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Table 1 values match the percentages quoted in the Results text (e.g. 19% for phiC31 on CtC attP3 x attB3; 18% and 50% for hCT1/hCT2 on TcT attR3 x attL3). No contradictory counts found.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label is a physical measurement — densitometry of DNA bands on a 1.2-1.25% agarose gel after NruI digestion, from triplicate in vitro reactions with purified protein. Not a model output, not computed from the features. AlphaFold3 is used only for illustrative structure figures, not for any label.

part_a_killers._stopped_at: A5 (with A3 also failing); per the checklist, scoring stops at the first failed killer.

existing_models.name: IntQuery (Bakalar et al., bioRxiv 2024, doi:10.1101/2024.10.10.617699) — a deep learning model predicting large serine integrase recombination activity at genomic off-target sites
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported Spearman correlation (rank correlation) of 0.42 under five-fold cross-validation, versus 0.34 for a linear regression trained the same way; trained on 410,776 cryptic attB (bacterial attachment) sequences measured by Cryptic-seq for Bxb1 integrase. Numbers from the preprint's search summary, not from running it.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation beyond Bxb1 to other integrases, and in vivo relevance of in vitro off-target activity.

existing_models.name: Model-guided attP sequence-activity model (Nat Commun 2022, doi:10.1038/s41467-022-31538-3) — machine-learning model computing Bxb1 inversion rate from attP attachment-site sequence
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; the abstract reports that reaction rates are well described by independent per-position nucleotide contributions, fitted to designed-and-sequenced attP libraries measured by quantitative PCR.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Extending position-independent models to sites far from the wild-type consensus.

existing_models.name: Durrant et al., Nat Biotechnol 2023 (doi:10.1038/s41587-022-01494-w) — computational discovery of thousands of large serine recombinases and prediction of their attachment-site specificity
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved in detail; reported as large-scale discovery plus specificity prediction across diverse integrases.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Predicting whether a given integrase can target an arbitrary site.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer or DNABERT-2 for the ~50 bp att sites; ESM-2 for the integrase protein sequences
backbone.hardware: CPU is ample for 4 proteins and ~10 DNA sites, but with 28 labels there is nothing to fit a head on — any embedding has more dimensions than the dataset has examples.
backbone.licence: Backbone licences are permissive/non-commercial and irrelevant here; the article itself is CC BY-NC.

integration.partner_dataset: Cryptic-seq / IntQuery off-target measurements (410,776 cryptic attB sequences for Bxb1) and the Durrant et al. integrase-attachment-site catalogue
integration.join_key: No usable key: this paper's hybrid integrases and synthetic hybrid att sites are novel constructs that exist in no public resource, and the partner data covers Bxb1, a different integrase clade.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written honestly — 28 measurements on two chimeric proteins against ~10 designed sites cannot be pooled with Bxb1 off-target libraries because the protein, the assay (in vitro plasmid deletion versus Cryptic-seq) and the readout differ.

controls.positive_control: Available in principle: wild-type phiC31 on its own attP x attB (76%) and wild-type TG1 on its own (89%) must score high, and both must score 0 on each other's sites — a textbook orthogonality result any method should recover.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=28; with 4 proteins and 8 site conditions, a shuffled model and a real model are statistically indistinguishable.
controls.external_validation: Farruggio and Calos (Biol Open 2014, doi:10.1242/bio.20148748) measured similar phiC31/TG1/phiBT1 chimeras in vivo in E. coli and HeLa cells, which is the nearest independent source — but it is a different assay with its own handful of qualitative readouts.

honest_claim_h3: Any model built on this would claim: 'across 28 in vitro gel measurements from one laboratory, recombination activity of two phiC31/TG1 chimeric integrases tracks which parent donated the DNA-binding domains' — which is exactly the conclusion the authors already state from the table by eye, with no model needed.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an integrase protein sequence and its DNA target site to predict how much DNA gets recombined.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered: for each pair of (integrase protein sequence, attachment-site DNA sequence), the protein and DNA sequence as input. Verified count of labelled examples: 28.
plain_idea.predict: The percentage of starting plasmid converted to recombined product, measured by quantifying DNA band brightness on an agarose gel after cutting with the NruI enzyme, averaged over three replicate reactions.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Genome-engineering groups want integrases that cut-and-paste DNA at a chosen genomic address rather than at a pre-installed landing pad; a sequence-to-activity model would let them design chimeras in silico. This paper, however, supplies 28 measurements, which is three orders of magnitude short of what that needs.

more_or_better_data.why: 28 measured recombination percentages here, against 410,776 cryptic attB sequences used to train IntQuery and designed attP libraries used in the Nat Commun 2022 model. This paper is four orders of magnitude smaller.

confidence_score.why: Triplicate standard deviations exist for each gel lane, so a noise estimate is technically available, but with 28 points you cannot calibrate per-prediction confidence for anything.

models_beatable.why: IntQuery's reported Spearman of 0.42 under five-fold cross-validation is modest and the split appears to be random rather than by sequence cluster, so it is beatable in principle — but with other data, not with this paper's 28 rows.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails every condition: the existing models cover Bxb1 rather than phiC31/TG1 chimeras, the assays differ (Cryptic-seq versus in vitro plasmid deletion on a gel), there is no shared split, and no join key links the two.

ml_idea: The project considered was a sequence-to-activity model mapping (integrase protein sequence, attachment-site DNA sequence) to percent recombination, so that new chimeric integrases and new target sites could be designed in silico. It is a genuinely valuable task, but this paper supplies 28 labelled measurements from one laboratory and one gel assay, with the DNA sequences only drawn inside figure images. The data belongs in a future pooled resource, not in a model on its own.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: the whole dataset is 28 numbers plus roughly ten ~50 bp DNA sequences and four ~600-residue protein sequences, so every step is seconds. The two hours is hand-transcription of Table 1 and of the att-site sequences out of the figure images.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the cells in Table 1. It took one minute and it killed the project: 32 cells, 4 of them 'ND', so 28 labelled measurements against a ~1,500-row threshold.

verdict_reason: A5 fails by roughly two orders of magnitude: the complete dataset is Table 1, 28 measured recombination percentages for 4 integrases across 8 attachment-site conditions, with no deposited files (data availability states everything is inside the article; Zenodo/Dryad return nothing; Europe PMC reports no supplement). A3 also fails in practice because the attachment-site DNA sequences — the only input that varies — exist only as letters drawn inside figure images. The biology is clean and the label is an honest physical measurement with stated units, so these numbers are worth contributing to a future pooled integrase sequence-activity resource, but they cannot support a model by themselves.
